selection_reasoning: These two tasks form a natural dependency chain. The player must first find smooth_sandstone_stairs, which are crafted from sandstone. In our scene, the smooth sandstone stairs will be placed near a sandstone structure. The logical flow is: the player needs to first locate and mine sandstone (the raw material), and then find the smooth_sandstone_stairs structure that is built nearby. However, a more compelling dependency is the reverse: the smooth_sandstone_stairs serve as a landmark/waypoint that guides the player to the sandstone deposit nearby. The player first finds the smooth_sandstone_stairs (a distinctive architectural feature), which leads them to the sandstone area where they can then mine sandstone. This creates a natural exploration-then-extraction flow where finding the stairs acts as a visual cue pointing toward the mineable sandstone resource.

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a 'find/locate' task — the player must navigate toward the smooth sandstone stairs and face them. Target is the center of the larger temple's stair crown at spawn-relative (9, 4, 12). With max_distance=10 (reduced from 16 per ValidatorAgent feedback), the player must walk at least 5-6 blocks from spawn before this can trigger, ensuring actual navigation occurred. facing_tolerance=60 ensures the player is looking toward the stairs, not just standing nearby.

Uses inventory_has because mining sandstone with any pickaxe drops the sandstone block as an item into the player's inventory. The player starts with no sandstone in inventory, so min_count=1 confirms they successfully mined at least one block. This is preferred over mine_block event tracking because inventory_has directly confirms the player obtained the resource. The wooden pickaxe provided is sufficient (mining level 0 can mine sandstone).

Behind it, a larger hollow sandstone temple (5x5x5, at ~7-11,0-3,10-14) is crowned with smooth sandstone stairs around its perimeter at y=4. Sand covers the ground beneath the structures. The player spawns on grass ~10 blocks away with a wooden pickaxe.
task_text: Find the smooth sandstone stairs on the desert temple structure, then mine sandstone blocks from the temple walls using your wooden pickaxe.
design_notes: Removed the dirt_path command (failed in sandbox). The scene works perfectly without it — grass provides a natural contrast to sand. Two structures provide redundant smooth_sandstone_stairs targets. The larger temple has thick sandstone walls (1 block thick after hollowing) that are easy to mine. Player spawns ~10 blocks from the smaller structure and ~15 blocks from the larger temple.
